name: Jaipur

setup.text: Put 3 camel cards face up between the players.
Shuffle the other cards. Deal 5 to each player. Draw 2 from the deck to bring the market to 5. Camels in the market are fine.
Sort the goods tokens by type into piles, highest value on top, spread so both players can see them.
Sort bonus tokens into 3 piles by sale size, shuffle each pile, and stack it face down. Put the camel token beside them.
Put the 3 Seals of Excellence within reach of both players.
Move any camels from your hand into a face-up herd in front of you.

turn.summary: Either take cards or sell cards. Never both.
steps: Take 1 goods card from the market and refill the gap from the deck.
Or exchange: take 2 or more goods from the market and give back the same number from your hand and/or herd. Returned cards may be camels or goods.
Or take all the camels from the market into your herd, then refill from the deck.
Or sell: choose one goods type and discard as many of that type as you like. Take one token of that type per card, highest first.
Sell 3 or more cards to also take a bonus token for that size.
End your turn with no more than 7 cards in hand.

round_end: The round ends at once when 3 goods token piles are empty, or when the deck cannot refill the market to 5.
The player with more camels takes the camel token. Equal camels means nobody does.
Turn over tokens and add them up. The richer player takes a Seal of Excellence.
end: The game ends when a player holds 2 Seals of Excellence. If nobody has 2 yet, set up again for another round; the loser of the last round starts.

scoring.text: Add up your goods tokens, bonus tokens and the camel token if you hold it.
Bonus tokens are worth 1-3 rupees for 3 cards sold, 4-6 for 4 cards, and 8-10 for 5 or more cards. The value is on the back only.

tiebreak: In a tied round, the player with more bonus tokens takes the seal, then the player with more goods tokens.

missed.text: When selling diamonds, gold or silver, you must sell at least 2 cards, even if only one token of that type is left.
You may sell only one goods type per turn.
If you take camels you must take every camel in the market, and you cannot mix camels with goods in the same take.
An exchange needs at least 2 cards. You cannot swap a single card, and you cannot return a goods type you are taking in the same exchange.
Camels do not count toward the 7 card hand limit.
If there are fewer tokens than cards sold, you still get the bonus token for the number of cards sold.

not_covered: Printed values of each goods token are on the tokens, not in the text.
